[h1]It Takes Two — Couple's Therapy, With Unnecessary Elephant Trauma[/h1]

I'll admit it: I started It Takes Two sceptical.

My usual taste leans towards gritty, realistic, and often brutal games like GTA V, Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order and Survivor, and Detroit: Become Human. So, naturally, this colourful, cartoonish adventure looked like a bit of a departure from my usual gaming diet.

But this was the first co-op game I played with my fiancée, and I'm SO glad I gave it a chance.

[b]THE STORY — MORE THAN JUST A CUTE LITTLE ADVENTURE[/b]

Beneath its colourful art style lies a genuinely heartfelt story about a relationship that's been falling apart for years. It explores love, frustration, resentment, and the difficult process of finding your way back to someone.

What really stood out to both of us was the ending. It doesn't magically fix years of broken trust and accumulated problems just because two people spend a few hours working together. But it shows that those hours can be a beginning. A first step towards something better.

And honestly? That hit harder than I expected from a game featuring talking household objects.

[b]THE GAMEPLAY — TWO BRAINCELLS, ONE OBJECTIVE[/b]

The gameplay is an absolute blast. Every level introduces new mechanics, abilities, and challenges that constantly change how you and your partner need to cooperate. Just when you've mastered one set of mechanics, the game throws something completely different at you.

Communication matters, teamwork matters, and sometimes you will absolutely blame your partner for your own spectacular failure. It's practically relationship counselling with platforming.

And that upside-down section? No spoilers, but we had a great time with that one.

[b]THE ELEPHANT — I WANT A LAWYER[/b]

If you've played it, you know.

If you haven't, I'm not spoiling it.

All I'll say is that I went into this game expecting a wholesome co-op adventure, and I came out carrying emotional damage caused by an elephant.

[b]THE VERDICT[/b]

It Takes Two surprised me in the best possible way. The story is heartfelt, the gameplay constantly stays fresh, and sharing the experience with my fiancée made it all the more special.

You don't need to be a fan of colourful platformers. You don't even need to think this is your kind of game.

Just find someone you love, grab a second controller, and give it a chance.

[b]9/10. One point deducted for the elephant incident. I will never financially or emotionally recover.[/b]
